**Unofficial connector, not affiliated with Tibber.** It brings your Tibber
account into Gladys: the hourly electricity prices of your home (today and
tomorrow), Tibber's price level, your consumption, and, with a Tibber Pulse
or Watty, the live power. Tibber is a trademark of Tibber AS. Available
where Tibber sells electricity: Norway, Sweden, Germany and the Netherlands.

Never tested with a real Tibber account or a real Pulse yet.

## What you get

| Surface                       | Content                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| ----------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| One device per **home**       | price now, next price, today's average, minimum and maximum (per kWh, VAT included), Tibber's level (very cheap to very expensive), a "cheap period" sensor, the 30-minute consumption for the Gladys energy monitoring, yesterday's consumption and cost |
| With a **Pulse / Watty**      | live power, production, today's consumption and cost, voltages and currents of the three phases                                                                                                                                                           |
| Scene triggers                | **cheap period started / ended** (the N cheapest hours of the day), **price level changed**, **tomorrow's prices published**, **live power crossed a mark** (500 W to 11 kW, up or down)                                                                  |
| Scene actions                 | **price now** (price, level, cheap hours, next price, today's figures, cheapest window) and **cheapest hours** (the cheapest N consecutive hours of the next 24 hours, today or tomorrow)                                                                 |
| Dashboard widgets             | **Tibber prices** (now, next, averages, level, cheapest hours, the curve of today and tomorrow) and **Tibber live power** (gauge, kWh and cost of the day, peak, voltages, currents)                                                                      |
| Energy contract (Gladys 5.2+) | a **Tibber** template per country: every half hour of your meter is priced from your Tibber hourly prices, plus the monthly subscription                                                                                                                  |

## Setup

1. On [developer.tibber.com](https://developer.tibber.com/settings/access-token),
   sign in with your Tibber account and create a **personal access token**.
2. Install the integration, paste the token in **Access token**, save, then
   click **Test the connection**: it lists your homes with their current
   price.
3. Open **Discovery** and add the device of each home.
4. Put the **Tibber prices** widget (and **Tibber live power** with a Pulse)
   on a dashboard, pick the home.

The prices are read at start and every hour; tomorrow's prices are asked
from 12:45 every 10 minutes until Tibber publishes them (around 13:00). The
sensors move at every price slot (hourly, or every 15 minutes where Tibber
moved to it). The consumption is read every hour.

## Scenes

- **Cheap period started / ended**: the current slot enters or leaves the N
  cheapest hours of the day (N = **Cheap hours per day**, 4 by default).
  Start the water heater, the car charger, the washing machine.
- **Price level changed**: Tibber's own level of the price (against the
  average of the last days) changed; filter on the new levels.
- **Tomorrow's prices published**: once a day, with the average, the
  extremes and the cheapest window of tomorrow, ready for a notification.
- **Live power crossed a mark**: the power of the Pulse went above or below
  the chosen number of watts. Warn when the oven and the charger run at the
  same time.

Two scene actions for a condition or a message that follows: **price now**
gives `price`, `level`, `cheap`, `next_price`, `avg_price`,
`window_start_time`…; **cheapest hours** gives the start and end
(`start_time`, `end_time`, `start` and `end` as ISO dates for a "wait
until"), `minutes_until_start` and the saving against the period. The
following actions of the scene find them in their variable list (written
`{{<step>.<action>.<key>}}`, for instance `{{0.0.price}}` when this action
is the first of the scene).

## Energy monitoring (Gladys 5.2 or newer)

In **Energy monitoring → Contracts**, create a contract from the **Tibber**
template of your country, pick the Tibber home device as the meter, and fill
in the monthly subscription. Gladys then asks the integration to price
every half hour from your own Tibber price history (energy price, VAT
included); the costs appear next to the consumption like any contract. The
**consumption** of the device is the hourly consumption Tibber reports,
split in two equal halves, published with about one hour of delay. It is the
only data of the device the energy monitoring counts: yesterday's and
today's consumption are plain sensors (in kWh) for display and scenes, never
added a second time.

If you own a Pulse, Gladys also shows the live power and today's cost
straight from Tibber.

Gladys 5.2.0 or newer is required.

### Devices created with version 0.1.1

Version 0.1.1 published yesterday's and today's consumption in features of
the "daily consumption" type (`yesterday_consumption`, `today_consumption`).
The costs and charts of the energy monitoring never used them (they read the
30-minute consumption), but these daily kWh could be added to the 30-minute
consumption in the weekly digest and in the answers of the Gladys MCP
server.

Gladys does not touch a created device until you click **Update**: until
then, the two old features stay, with their history, but receive nothing
any more. To move to the new sensors, open **Discovery**, then the Tibber
device (badge **Already added**), and click **Update**. Gladys then adds
`yesterday_kwh` and `today_kwh`, removes the two old features, and keeps the
device, the history of every other feature (30-minute consumption and its
cost, prices, costs) and the link with your energy contract. A scene or a
dashboard chart set on one of the two old features must be pointed at
`yesterday_kwh` or `today_kwh`.

## Troubleshooting

- **"Tibber refused the access token"**: the token was revoked or mistyped;
  create a new one on developer.tibber.com. A refused token is not sent
  again, even after a restart, until you save the configuration (saving tries
  once more, even with the same token).
- **"Tibber asked to slow down (429)"**: no call at all until the time shown
  (Tibber's Retry-After, between 1 minute and 6 hours, kept across a
  restart); the last values stay, then everything resumes by itself.
- **"No home with an active subscription"**: the account has no running
  Tibber contract yet.
- **No live power**: the home needs a Tibber Pulse or Watty with real-time
  consumption enabled in the Tibber app, and the **Live power** option on.
  The status line says "live power on \<home>" when the stream is connected.
- **Tomorrow's prices missing**: Tibber publishes them around 13:00 local
  time; the integration keeps asking every 10 minutes.
- Logs: the integration's log level is set with the `LOG_LEVEL` variable.

## Privacy

The token is kept by Gladys in its database (in clear, like every secret
field, its backups included), never shown again, and only sent to Tibber's
servers (`api.tibber.com`, `websocket-api.tibber.com`). Your address is only used to
name the device when the home has no nickname. The `/data` volume of the
integration holds only a random key, a keyed hash (HMAC) of a refused token
(never the token) and the end of a 429 pause.

## Konfigurationseinstellungen

Diese Einstellungen fragt Tibber in seinem Konfigurationsbildschirm in Gladys ab.

| Einstellung | Typ | Pflichtfeld | Beschreibung |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Tibber account | `section` | Nein | Unofficial connector, not affiliated with Tibber. Create a personal access token on developer.tibber.com (Settings → Access token) and paste it below: the integration discovers your homes, reads the hourly prices (today and tomorrow), your consumption, and, with a Tibber Pulse or Watty, the live power. It also offers a Tibber contract template for the Gladys energy monitoring. Tibber is a trademark of Tibber AS. |
| Access token | `secret` | Ja | Kept by Gladys in its database, never shown again, only sent to Tibber. |
| Cheap hours per day | `number` | Nein | The N cheapest hours of the day make the "cheap period" (sensor, triggers, widget). |
| Live power from a Tibber Pulse / Watty | `boolean` | Nein | Keeps a websocket open to Tibber for the homes with real-time consumption enabled. |

## So installierst du Tibber in Gladys

1. Öffne in Gladys **Integrationen**: Tibber erscheint im Katalog neben den nativen Integrationen, mit einem Community-Badge.
2. Klicke auf **Installieren**. Gladys lädt das Docker-Image (`ghcr.io/lm1lc3n7/gladys-tibber:0.1.4`) herunter, startet es in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox und erzeugt die Oberfläche der Integration (Geräte, Erkennung und Konfiguration).
3. Öffne den Bildschirm **Konfiguration** der Integration, fülle die Einstellungen aus und speichere.
4. Du kannst sie auch direkt über die URL ihres Repositorys installieren: [https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-tibber](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7/gladys-tibber).

Tibber benötigt Gladys `>=5.2.0`. Der Katalog in Gladys wird stündlich aktualisiert, eine neue Version ist also spätestens eine Stunde nach ihrer Veröffentlichung verfügbar.

Du nutzt Gladys noch nicht? Es ist kostenlos und Open Source: [folge der Installationsanleitung](/de/docs/), um loszulegen.

## Über externe Integrationen

Tibber ist eine **externe Integration**: eine Community-Integration, die als Docker-Container verpackt und auf GitHub veröffentlicht wird. Gladys installiert sie mit einem Klick und führt sie in einer vom Kern isolierten Sandbox aus. Sie wird von [LM1LC3N7](https://github.com/LM1LC3N7) veröffentlicht und gepflegt, nicht vom Gladys-Kernteam.
